answer: Each agent account must lock a scarce token deposit before it can submit work, and the protocol releases that deposit only after independent peers verify the result. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must lock a hundred deposits and keep them tied up through review. If any account is caught double-claiming or colluding, its deposit is slashed. Whether work is routed through an island, mesa, or reef, the same bond makes fake identities costly rather than merely numerous.
